prompt.en: A station is transmitting on 7 MHz and a 14 MHz harmonic is measured in the accessory rack. Which change would NOT help keep harmonic energy out of station wiring?

text.en: Move the low-pass filter to the antenna side of the tuner so the accessories see the harmonic first
Install the low-pass filter at the final RF output before the accessory rack
Use a short jumper from the final RF output to the filter input
Choose a filter whose cutoff passes 7 MHz but attenuates the 14 MHz harmonic

explanation.en: Putting the filter after the tuner leaves more station wiring carrying the harmonic. The helpful changes all make the filter act earlier or make sure it rejects the harmonic frequency.

prompt.en: Spot the error in this FM-transmitter note: “The speech amplifier feeds audio to a multiplier; after the oscillator is tripled, the audio variations appear as FM at the output.”

text.en: A multiplier erases any frequency deviation that was already present on the oscillator signal
The power amplifier should lower the oscillator centre frequency before speech is applied
The audio must vary the oscillator before multiplication; a multiplier cannot create voice deviation from audio it never receives
The microphone should generate the RF carrier directly so the multiplier has voice-frequency input

explanation.en: In an FM chain the audio deviation is applied to the oscillator first. Later multiplier stages move that already frequency-varying RF signal to the needed carrier frequency.

prompt.en: A receiver uses a 10.700 MHz IF and a local oscillator above a 144.390 MHz signal. What local oscillator frequency should you expect?

explanation.en: With high-side injection, add the IF: 144.390 MHz + 10.700 MHz = 155.090 MHz.
